title: Linux Root Filesystem 100% Full
symptom: Applications crash, services fail to write logs, and shell warns: 'No space left on device'.
initial_observations: df -h shows / mounted on /dev/xvda1 is at 100% capacity (0 bytes available).
Command line tab completion and temporary files fail.

possible_causes.cause: Unrotated or runaway log files in /var/log
possible_causes.evidence_needed: du -sh /var/log/* reveals single log file tens of gigabytes in size.
possible_causes.remediation: Truncate runaway log file (`> /var/log/app.log`) and configure proper logrotate policy.

possible_causes.cause: Deleted large files still held open by a running process
possible_causes.evidence_needed: lsof +L1 shows unlinked files holding open file descriptors with non-zero size.
possible_causes.remediation: Restart the process holding the file descriptor open or truncate via `/proc/$PID/fd/$FD`.

investigation_steps.title: Check Disk Capacity by Mount Point
investigation_steps.explanation: Identify exactly which filesystem mount is exhausted.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Mount point showing 100% Use% and 0 Available.

investigation_steps.title: Identify Top Storage-Consuming Directories
investigation_steps.explanation: Recursively isolate which top-level directory contains the excess data.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Directory consuming disproportionate volume of disk space.

investigation_steps.title: Detect Deleted Files Held Open by Processes
investigation_steps.explanation: When rm is run on an open file, space is not released until process closes the file handle.
investigation_steps.what_to_look_for: Process name and large size associated with (deleted) file.

verification: Execute `df -h /` and verify Use% is below 80%.
prevention: Configure logrotate with size caps and compression.
Set up CloudWatch disk metric alarms using CloudWatch agent.
